title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operating in autonomous mode struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas. A human safety operator was present in the vehicle but did not intervene to prevent the collision. The vehicle did not slow down or stop upon encountering the animal.

This incident shows a failure in object detection or response planning. The system either did not identify the duck as an obstacle requiring avoidance, or it identified it but did not generate a stopping or swerving command. A human safety operator with authority to override could have prevented the outcome, but the operator either did not perceive the hazard or did not act in time.

Avride stated that vehicle data showed the car stopped appropriately at all relevant stop signs and disputed a separate allegation about a stop sign violation. Whether the presence of a duck on pavement presents conditions the system was designed to handle, or whether operator response time was adequate to the scenario, is not established by the reporting.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An Avride autonomous vehicle struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, making it familiar to residents, which intensified their concerns about autonomous vehicle safety in the area.

In response to the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode and investigated the claims. The company disputed a resident's assertion that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, stating it reviewed vehicle data and found the car stopped appropriately at all relevant signs. Avride has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets near the lake and is now conducting simulation experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar incidents. Meanwhile, local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator, and multiple autonomous vehicle companies continue testing in Austin.
